subject: KMS/HSM economics — seat vs. usage split and invoice mapping
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Bates <jordan.b@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: KMS/HSM economics — seat vs. usage split and invoice mapping

Jordan — thanks again for the time this morning. Attached is a compact breakdown of the two packaging options we talked through: (A) HSM seat + usage blend, and (B) usage-only with reservation credits. I kept the spreadsheet focused on annualized economics and invoice mapping so your FP&A can see how charges would flow between the platform seat fee, HSM seat amortization, and per-call usage.

High level:
- Option A (Seat + Usage): one-time HSM seat fee amortized monthly + lower per-call charge for HSM-backed keys. Better for predictable volume.
- Option B (Usage-only): no upfront seat, higher per-call HSM premium but credits if volume exceeds threshold. Better if you want OPEX-only.

Notes in the sheet include a 12-month amortization baseline and a 36-month alternative (tab 2) — we can shift as you prefer. Also flagged the items that require legal sign-off (data residency addendum and HSM terms).

Attachments: kms_hsm_pricing_breakdown_v2.xlsx, clearhealth_sow_v1.pdf

Next steps: can you share whether your procurement prefers capitalization (capex) of the seat or OPEX? That will change the recommendation. If you want, we can ship a blended proposal that amortizes the seat over 24 months and offers a 10% volume credit on month 13+.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Vanessa — thanks for the sheet. A few follow-ups from procurement and FP&A:

1) Can you show a side-by-side ARR and cash-flow impact if we capitalise the seat (12-month amort) vs expense it? FP&A will look at cash in 2027 vs 2028.
2) For Option B (usage-only), what does the volume credit look like if we hit 2x baseline? Is it a retroactive credit or future-month credit?
3) Audit log retention — we need a pricing line for 7-year retention exported monthly (EU residency not needed for this account).

Can you loop in legal for the residency/HSM language and Monica for implementation timelines? We want to finalize commercial terms by EOW (Friday).

Regards,

To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Bates <jordan.b@clearhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@clearhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: KMS/HSM economics — seat vs. usage split and invoice mapping

Aditya / Monica — forwarding Jordan's ask. Procurement wants: cash vs ARR view (capex amortized 12mo vs expense), clarity on whether credits are retroactive, and an explicit line for 7-year audit-log retention export.

Aditya — can you run a quick cash/ARR two-column for the 12- and 24-month amort scenarios? Put the numbers in the existing spreadsheet (tab 'FP&A views'). Monica — can you estimate implementation lead times for the HSM onboarding (incl. key rotation window) and whether the audit export for 7-year retention is feasible as a monthly export. I called out the legal bits in red in the sheet.

My recommended commercial compromise to propose to the customer:
- HSM seat amortized over 24 months (midpoint) with a 7% commit credit applied to seat amortization if they sign a 12-month committed usage tier for HSM calls.
- Volume achievement (2x baseline) triggers a retroactive credit applied to the most recent billing cycle (not a future-only credit).
- Audit log export priced at $0.04 per exported 1k events per month, with a 20% discount if they prepay 12 months.

Attachments: kms_hsm_pricing_breakdown_v2.xlsx

If legal signs off on the wording, we'll present the blended proposal to Jordan late Tuesday.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Bates <jordan.b@clearhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: KMS/HSM economics — seat vs. usage split and invoice mapping

Vanessa — reviewed the sheet and the proposed commercial compromise. A couple of legal redlines / clarifications before we present:

1) "Retroactive credit": we can agree to a retroactive credit but limit lookback to 90 days from the date of volume qualification to avoid open-ended adjustments. Suggest language: "Retroactive credits will be applied to invoices issued within 90 days of qualification date."
2) Audit export pricing: add explicit SLA for export availability (99.9% monthly) and an upper bound on data egress costs — we will cap Redwood's billed export fee at a 10% of actual egress charges if the customer provides cloud egress receipts.
3) HSM seat termination: define pro-rated refund schedule if the seat is decommissioned before amortization completes (reduce refund for consumed amortization).

Also attached a DocuSign-ready clause set (I can paste if needed) — link below. If you're presenting the blended proposal, include these guardrails; procurement typically pushes back on retroactive infinite credits.

Markus Klein
Sr. Counsel | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: KMS/HSM economics — seat vs. usage split and invoice mapping

Team — thanks, appreciate the speed. ClearHealth is comfortable with the blended proposal under these adjustments: 24-month amortization, 7% seat credit tied to a 12-month usage commit, and the 90-day cap on retroactive credits.

Two asks before we sign:
1) Please add a line item on the SOW that maps the seat amort to a dedicated invoice description (we want it to hit 'Platform Services — HSM seat' on our chart of accounts).
2) Confirm the audit export SLA and the conditional egress cap language — procurement needs the sentence exactly as written for our internal approvals.

If you can get a DocuSign bundle with those two bullets + the SOW line item, procurement will sign and we can target onboarding starting 7/20.

Jordan
